newsitem.title: CHINA: Central China rains create excess power generation.
newsitem.headline: Central China rains create excess power generation.

text.p: Heavy rainfall in central China has boosted hydroelectric output and created an historic surplus of electricity in the region, the Xinhua news agency said on Monday.
Autumn and winter rains pushed up electricity generation by a year-on-year 10 percent at major hydropower plants in China's central power grid, Xinhua said.
Hydroelectric power stations made up two thirds of the grid's generating plants, the agency said.
A drop in power demand from local enterprises and eastern China's power network had also contributed to the region's first-ever energy surplus, it said.
The grid covered Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi and Henan provinces and had a total generating capacity of 32,300 megawatts and an annual output of 150 million megawatt-hours, it said.
Most other parts of China were suffering severe shortages of electricity, it said without elaborating.
China has been saddled with chronic energy shortages as rapid economic growth and a booming industrial sector have put increasing demands on its power industry.
